title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Page 790 of the continuation of 'La Longue Marche', section 9°, 'Retour aux M_{ρ,σ}'. Previous pages compute, over a base S_0, a family of affine group schemes attached to two 'symmetries' ρ and σ. These are a normaliser N_ρ, a normaliser N_σ (with a variant N_σ^♮), a centraliser Z_{ρ,σ} and a group G_{ρ,σ} (with a variant G^♮_{ρ,σ}). Each surjects onto a common quotient γ = γ_{ρ,σ} = Ω_12^* (written 𝕆_12^* on the neighbouring pages). The preceding page gives semidirect decompositions such as N_σ^♮ ≅ 𝕆_12^*·G_a and N_σ ≅ 𝕆_12^*·(L_σ × G_a). There 𝕆_12^* acts on G_a through a character χ: 𝕆_12^* → G_m, and on L_σ through a sign ε_2: 𝕆_12^* → (±1)_{S_0}.

On this page Grothendieck says he is following §49 (VI, 5°). He then defines the groups of interest as iterated fibre products over γ:
- (183) M_{ρ,σ} = N_ρ ×_γ N_σ ×_γ G_{ρ,σ}, and the analogous M^♮_{ρ,σ} built from the ♮-variants.
- (184) Γ_{ρ,σ} = N_ρ ×_γ N_σ.
- (182)/(184) 'S'-versions (So M, So M^♮, So Γ) obtained by adding one more factor Z_{ρ,σ} ×_γ.

He then remarks that the S-versions are only technical auxiliaries. Each is an extension of the corresponding group without S by L_0^M = Ker(Z_{ρ,σ} → Ω_12^*) ≅ G_a. Concretely, So Γ_{ρ,σ} is an extension of Γ_{ρ,σ} by L_0^M, and So M, So M^♮ are its pullbacks along the epimorphisms M_{ρ,σ} → Γ_{ρ,σ} and M^♮_{ρ,σ} → Γ_{ρ,σ}. Attention is then directed to the groups without S. The next page relates them by commutative diagrams of exact sequences 1 → 𝔊^± → M^{(♮)}_{ρ,σ} → Γ_{ρ,σ} → 1, and by 1 → SN_ρ × SZ_σ → Γ_{ρ,σ} → 𝕆_12^* → 1, compared with p. 639 (79).

The page serves a bookkeeping purpose. It packages several groups sharing the quotient 𝕆_12^* into one 'stabiliser' group scheme M_{ρ,σ}, whose structure (kernel, semidirect splittings) is then read off. This belongs to Grothendieck's description of automorphism/stabiliser groups at special points in the Teichmüller-tower part of the Longue Marche. The precise geometric meaning of ρ, σ and Ω_12 cannot be fully pinned down from this page alone.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The construction is formal: fibre products over a common quotient, plus pullback of an extension.
The kernel claim needs Z_{ρ,σ} → Ω_12^* to be surjective with kernel G_a. That is consistent with the decomposition Z_{ρ,σ} ≅ 𝕆_12^*·G_0 (G_a) on the next page, so the claim is fine.
Minor gap: 'So Γ' as an extension of Γ by L_0^M follows from the fibre-product definition only if Z_{ρ,σ} → γ is an epimorphism. This is assumed implicitly.

ideas.what: Defining a composite stabiliser group scheme as the fibre product over a common quotient γ = Ω_12^* of normalisers N_ρ, N_σ and a group G_{ρ,σ}
ideas.modern_name: fibre product of group schemes over a common quotient (pullback of extensions)

ideas.what: Auxiliary 'S' groups as extensions by L_0^M = Ker(Z_{ρ,σ}→Ω_12^*) ≅ G_a, obtained by pulling back along epimorphisms M → Γ
ideas.modern_name: pullback (Baer) of a group extension along a homomorphism

deep.surprise_reason: The page is purely technical bookkeeping within a long computation. It contains no new conceptual idea or result beyond fibre products and pulled-back extensions.
transcription_corrections: The superscript transcribed '⊊' on N_σ, M_{ρ,σ} and G_{ρ,σ} is the same decoration as '♮'/'⇆' on the neighbouring pages (a variant marker), not a strict-inclusion sign.
The superscript '?' on N_ρ is a variant marker as on the next page; it does not mean uncertainty about the exponent.
'So M' is most likely 'S M' (or 'S_o'), matching the 'S Z_σ', 'S N_ρ' notation of the adjacent pages.
Ω_12^* corresponds to 𝕆_12^* in the neighbouring transcriptions.
Page number 790 is written at the top, next to the heading.
